title: rate_per_sec accepts non-integer JSON literals (1e2, 100.0, 1.0e1, -0); -0 is echoed back as -0
evidence: PUT {"rate_per_sec":1e2,"reason":"abc"} -> 200, sets=[100]. Same for 100.0, 1E2, 10000.00. -0 -> 200 with override.rate_per_sec:-0, paused:true. Contract 3.2 says JSON integer. 0.3, 10001, -1, 1e400, 99999999999999999999, strings, null, bool, unknown field, trailing data, 4 KiB body are all correctly 400 with no write.
fix: In parseRate accept only ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$ and use ParseInt, or state in the contract that integral-valued numbers are accepted; normalise -0 to 0.

title: Auditor panic after the Redis apply: override stays applied, but no ERROR line with actor/action/subject/reason and no audit:"failed" response
evidence: panicAuditor -> panic leaves OpsOverride.Set; store sets=[0] (pause applied); log has no level=ERROR line. In production httpx.Recover turns it into a 500, so the UI says 'not sent, retry' while the pause is live and unaudited.
fix: recover() inside OpsOverride.audit and treat a panic as AuditFailed with the same ERROR log line.

title: Response is not built from the stored value when the read-back says the override is gone (concurrent DELETE) or fails: it returns active:true with the request value
evidence: Store that is cleared right after the HSET: response {override:{active:true,rate_per_sec:120},audit:recorded} while store.active=false; audit row ADMIT_OVERRIDE_SET with rate 120. 20 concurrent PUTs otherwise behave: 20 sets, 20 audit rows, last write wins.
fix: When the read-back is inactive, answer with what was read (active:false, rate null); or do set + read in one Lua script / MULTI.

title: Mandatory reason can be visually empty: three zero-width spaces pass the 3..200 check on server and client
evidence: Server: reason "\u200b\u200b\u200b" -> 200, audit reason stored as three ZWSP. Client: clearAdmitOverride(EV, "\u200b\u200b\u200b") sends the request. Control characters inside the reason are accepted too. Length rules are otherwise right: 200 runes ok, 201 -> 400, "  ab  " -> 400.
repro:
opsCall(rig.mux, http.MethodPut, ovPath(opsEvent), "ops", `{"rate_per_sec":5,"reason":"\u200b\u200b\u200b"}`) // 200, rig.aud.entries[0].Reason == "\u200b\u200b\u200b"
// web (vitest): await clearAdmitOverride(EV, "\u200b\u200b\u200b") resolves
fix: Strip format/control runes (Cf, Cc) before counting, in NormalizeReason and normalizeOverrideReason.

title: Encoded dot-segments are not normalised: a buyer's GET /v1/assistant/%2e%2e/ops/ai/mode matches the Public /v1/assistant/ route and is forwarded (pre-existing; no bypass today)
evidence: Gateway fixture, buyer token: 200, upstream 'assistant' was reached with X-Identity-Role=buyer. Not exploitable now: ai-worker returns 404 for the encoded form, a Go ServeMux upstream keeps %2e%2e as a literal segment, and all three services re-check the role. Plain '..' and '//' are redirected and end in 403. Everything else in the role matrix held: buyer/organizer/moderator 403 without reaching upstream, ops 403 on sales, other methods 404, spoofed X-Identity-Role ignored, /admin/mode 404.
fix: Reject at the gateway any request whose EscapedPath contains %2e or %2f (case-insensitive) before routing.

title: Web trusts 200 bodies: missing `audit` is shown as recorded; malformed bodies throw a raw TypeError instead of OpsWriteError / a degraded source / ApiError
evidence: PUT 200 {override:{active:true,rate_per_sec:0},paused:true} -> audit:'recorded'. PUT 200 {} -> TypeError (no code, UI shows generic retry although the command was applied). Queue 200 without `override` -> getOpsWarRoom rejects with TypeError, so the whole snapshot is lost instead of waitingroom being 'unavailable'. Sales 200 without `totals` -> TypeError.
fix: Validate wire shapes: audit !== 'recorded' -> 'failed'; shape errors -> OpsWriteError('UNAVAILABLE') / SourceError(0) / ApiError.

title: A plain 401 on a write is reported as 'Không có quyền'; a plain 401 on a read source is only 'unavailable'; neither sends the user to login
evidence: PUT -> 401 /problems/unauthorized: OpsWriteError code FORBIDDEN. Queue -> 401 /problems/unauthorized: sources.waitingroom='unavailable', no OpsServiceError(401). Sales 401 -> generic 'Không tải được doanh số'. Only the token-expired/refresh path yields AUTH_REQUIRED.
fix: Map HTTP 401 to the auth-required path in getJson, sendOverride and getRealtimeSales.

title: Ownership check is a case-sensitive string compare of organizer_id::text with X-Identity-Id
evidence: Owner presenting the same UUID in upper case -> 404. Only bites if a token ever carries a non-lowercase sub. The attacks that matter held: other organizer reading through a cache warmed by the owner -> 404 with 1 query; ops role on sales -> 403; 10 concurrent inventory calls -> 1 query; role is checked before the UUID.
repro:
r := baseReader(); r.sales.OrganizerID = organizerA; mux := newOpsMux(r)
opsGet(mux, salesPath(opsEv), strings.ToUpper(organizerA), "organizer").Code // 404
fix: strings.EqualFold, or lowercase the principal id before comparing.

title: ai-worker role check trims whitespace and accepts any non-empty identity id (the Go services reject both)
evidence: X-Identity-Role ' ops ' -> 200; X-Identity-Id 'anything-not-uuid' -> 200. Go authx answers 401 to 'ops ' and to a non-UUID id. Correct otherwise: OPS/buyer/missing role -> 403, missing or blank id -> 401, problem+json with no-store, other methods 405, values equal /admin/mode.
repro:
client.get('/v1/ops/ai/mode', headers={'X-Identity-Id': ID, 'X-Identity-Role': ' ops '}).status_code  # 200
client.get('/v1/ops/ai/mode', headers={'X-Identity-Id': 'anything-not-uuid', 'X-Identity-Role': 'ops'}).status_code  # 200
fix: Compare the role without strip() and require a UUID-shaped id, mirroring authx.PrincipalFromHeaders.

title: suspicion: a typed-nil Auditor defeats the `auditor == nil` fail-closed check (not reachable from main.go today)
evidence: NewOpsOverride(store, (*fakeAuditor)(nil), log): PUT applies the override (sets=[0]) and then panics with a nil pointer dereference. NewAuditorFromEnv returns an untyped nil, so production is safe; the guard relies on every future caller doing the same.
repro:
var typed *fakeAuditor
httpadapter.NewOpsHandler(&fakeState{}, app.NewOpsOverride(st, typed, log), log).Routes(mux)
opsCall(mux, http.MethodPut, ovPath(opsEvent), "ops", `{"rate_per_sec":0,"reason":"abc"}`) // sets=[0], then panic
fix: Covered by the recover proposed in X-2.
